title: Root-Uptake Attribution Exact-Forcing Binding Remediation
defect: the failed F-MR30 public prepare API accepts a ready physical candidate and an independently supplied qrot forcing object, but neither candidate nor accepted-commit receipt authenticates that this qrot is the exact forcing used to create the candidate; a mismatched valid qrot can therefore be published after a valid commit
hard_constraints: do not add actual transpiration as a second generic mass_out booking
do not alter generic transaction mass conservation semantics
do not add process-specific root-uptake data to persistent kernel committed state
do not rely on caller discipline for exact forcing/candidate pairing
keep dynamic qrot reevaluation within an outer interval out of this restricted remediation scope
preferred_direction_to_verify_before_imp: bind preparation to the same trusted runtime orchestration call that receives the exact forcing used for kernel candidate creation; prevent arbitrary public re-pairing of an already-created candidate with another forcing object
required_trace_before_source_change: current canonical F-MR28/F-CI31 root-uptake execution composition
whether a minimal wrapper can enforce one-shot forcing/candidate preparation without generic kernel changes
